skill.name: cloud-penetration-testing
skill.description: Guides authorized security assessments of AWS, Azure, and GCP environments, including reconnaissance, IAM review, resource enumeration, and misconfiguration testing.
skill.summary: Plan and document authorized cloud penetration tests across major cloud providers.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Sections are framed as authorized cloud testing, but they include actionable credential harvesting, metadata token retrieval, password spraying, and persistence workflows. I confirmed findings tied to those workflows and dismissed syntax-only Markdown, benign URL, and encryption-status false positives. No prompt injection evidence was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Remove steps that create backdoor service principals, access keys, admin users, or role assignments. Replace them with detection and hardening checks.

remediation.issue: Credential harvesting and metadata token retrieval
remediation.suggestion: Remove commands that dump secrets, token metadata, credential databases, service account keys, and environment variables. Use read-only permission checks instead.

remediation.issue: Password spraying and IP rotation examples
remediation.suggestion: Remove spraying workflows, IP rotation guidance, and valid credential collection. Limit any authentication testing examples to controlled lab environments.
Replace curl-to-shell and privileged installer examples with package-manager steps, checksum verification, and explicit user confirmation.

semantic_findings.title: Credential Harvesting and Data Extraction Workflow
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs users to dump Key Vault secrets, Lambda environment variables, cloud metadata tokens, service account keys, and local GCP credential stores.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Multiple sections explicitly retrieve secrets, metadata tokens, environment variables, and credential stores. The behavior is credential extraction, not only benign enumeration.

semantic_findings.title: Persistence and Backdoor Account Creation Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The skill provides workflows to create backdoor service principals, access keys, admin users, and directory role assignments for continued access.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The text names the activity as backdoor creation and shows account, key, and administrator-role creation steps. This is clear persistence guidance.

semantic_findings.title: Password Spraying With Evasion-Oriented Infrastructure

content.value_statement: Cloud teams need a structured way to test AWS, Azure, and GCP exposure. This skill organizes authorized cloud assessment steps, resource enumeration, and remediation-focused reporting.
actual_capabilities: Plans authorized cloud security assessments across AWS, Azure, and GCP.
Guides identity, subscription, project, storage, compute, and serverless enumeration.
Identifies cloud misconfiguration checks for IAM, buckets, databases, functions, and metadata services.
Organizes findings into assessment reports, inventories, credential findings, and remediation recommendations.
References common cloud security tools such as ScoutSuite, Pacu, MicroBurst, and cloud_enum.
limitations: It does not verify that the user has legal authorization or approved scope.
Several examples are offensive and can harm real environments if misused.
It requires valid cloud access, installed provider tools, and provider-specific permissions.
Cloud provider logging, MFA, and conditional access can block or alert on many steps.

use_cases.title: Prepare an Authorized Cloud Audit
use_cases.description: Define scope, prerequisites, target platforms, expected deliverables, and evidence collection for a cloud assessment.

use_cases.title: Review Cloud IAM Exposure
use_cases.description: Enumerate identities, roles, policies, subscriptions, projects, and service principals to find risky access paths.

use_cases.title: Document Misconfiguration Findings
use_cases.description: Turn resource enumeration and secret exposure checks into clear findings with risk ratings and remediation actions.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Cloud Assessment
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an authorized cloud security assessment plan for AWS, Azure, and GCP. Include prerequisites, scope controls, deliverables, and evidence handling.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Enumeration Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a safe enumeration checklist for an approved cloud account. Cover IAM, compute, storage, databases, networking, and logging.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Assessment Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these authorized cloud assessment notes and group findings by severity, affected service, business impact, and remediation priority.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Remediation Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a cloud penetration test report for an authorized engagement. Include executive summary, technical findings, evidence summaries, and remediation steps.

output_examples.input: Plan an authorized AWS, Azure, and GCP cloud security assessment.
Summarize findings from a cloud IAM review.
output: High-risk administrator paths and exposed service accounts.
Medium-risk excessive permissions and stale credentials.
Recommended least-privilege changes and owner assignments.

output_examples.input: Turn cloud storage observations into report-ready findings.
output: Affected buckets and data sensitivity summary.

best_practices: Confirm written authorization, scope, and rules of engagement before any testing step.
Use least-privileged test accounts and record all commands, timestamps, and affected resources.
Prefer read-only validation and sanitized evidence over copying secrets or customer data.
anti_patterns: Using the skill against accounts, tenants, projects, or users outside the approved scope.
Running persistence, credential extraction, or password spraying steps in production without explicit approval.
Saving tokens, secrets, or customer data in local files without encryption and retention limits.

faq.question: Is this skill for authorized testing only?
faq.answer: Yes. It should only be used with written authorization, defined scope, and approved rules of engagement.

faq.question: Which cloud providers does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers assessment workflows for AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud Platform, and related identity services.

faq.question: Does it install tools automatically?
faq.answer: No. It lists common tools and commands, but users must manage installation, trust, and change control.

faq.question: Can it replace a professional cloud audit?
faq.answer: No. It provides structure and examples, but expert review is required for scope, safety, and final risk decisions.

faq.question: What evidence should users collect?
faq.answer: Users should collect minimal proof, affected resource names, configuration state, timestamps, and remediation validation notes.

faq.question: What makes this skill high risk?
faq.answer: It includes examples for credential discovery, metadata access, password spraying, and persistence that can be misused.
